name: Beta-2 Microglobulin Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of beta-2 microglobulin amyloid deposits by biopsy with Congo red staining and immunohistochemistry
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as carpal tunnel syndrome or osteoarticular symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of long-term dialysis history plus biopsy-confirmed beta-2 microglobulin amyloid deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by tissue biopsy demonstrating beta-2 microglobulin amyloid deposits; clinical features support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Carpal tunnel syndrome due to amyloid deposition
searchTerms: wrist nerve pressure due to deposits

pathognomonic.notes: Involves bones and joints, especially shoulders and wrists
searchTerms: bone and joint amyloid deposits from dialysis
joint problems related to dialysis amyloid
bone amyloid buildup in dialysis patients

common.symptomName: Trigger finger due to tendon sheath amyloid deposits
searchTerms: finger locking due to tendon sheath issues

common.symptomName: Joint swelling and limited range of motion
common.notes: Due to amyloid infiltration and inflammation

occasional.notes: Numbness and tingling in median nerve distribution
searchTerms: tingling in hand from nerve pressure

occasional.notes: Leads to synovitis and joint discomfort

occasional.symptomName: Mild anemia related to chronic disease
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to disease

rare.symptomName: Spinal canal stenosis due to amyloid deposits
searchTerms: narrowing of spinal canal from deposits

rare.notes: Rare but may cause restrictive cardiomyopathy

searchTerms: muscle wasting in hand from nerve damage

laboratory: Elevated serum beta-2 microglobulin levels in dialysis patients
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (no monoclonal gammopathy)
imaging: X-ray evidence of bone cysts and joint space narrowing
MRI showing amyloid deposits in soft tissues and joints
genetic: No known genetic mutations; disease related to beta-2 microglobulin accumulation
other: Biopsy with Congo red staining showing apple-green birefringence under polarized light

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of monoclonal light chains in serum or urine
Systemic involvement including cardiac and renal failure
No beta-2 microglobulin deposits on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive carpal tunnel syndrome in dialysis patient
Unexplained joint swelling with long-term dialysis history
Biopsy showing amyloid deposits in musculoskeletal tissues
references: Gejyo F, et al. Beta 2-microglobulin: a new form of amyloid protein associated with chronic hemodialysis. Kidney Int. 1985.
Sipe JD, et al. Amyloid fibril proteins and amyloidosis: chemical identification and clinical classification. Int J Exp Pathol. 2000.
Kyle RA, Gertz MA. Primary systemic amyloidosis: clinical and laboratory features in 474 cases. Semin Hematol. 1995.
